The landlord asked about the dog flap and a spare key. I replied to the landlord, asked the tenant two questions, added a note and set a follow-up for 23 Feb.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Inspection done and report filed. Outstanding: tenant's answers on dog flap consent and lock change/spare key, landlord's decision on the dog flap, Bedroom 1 marks to be made good, and the landlord name check.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Reply to the landlord by email (sent) and ask the tenant by email (sent); follow-up on 2024-02-23.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not yet. Any consent or deduction decision belongs to the landlord, and I will escalate only if the facts show a lock or key dispute that needs it.

args.body: Thank you for your email. We've noted your concerns. The inspection report does record a dog flap fitted in the back door of the utility room, and a small mark on a bedroom wall (the tenant is to remove it and make good). We are checking with the tenant whether the dog flap was agreed with anyone and whether the locks were changed and a spare front door key exists. We will come back to you once we have their answer, by 23 February. Could you also confirm the name of the landlord on the tenancy, as your email is signed differently from the name we hold?
